# Physical model overview {.unnumbered #physical-model-overview}

## Calculation sequence {#physical-calculation-sequence}

The ACC Magnetometer calculation has four conceptual stages:

1. Construct optical-pumping and relaxation generators for every active alkali.
2. Solve the zero-RF steady ground-state populations.
3. Linearize the density-matrix dynamics with respect to a weak RF field.
4. Apply optical readout operators and, for a physical pump, close the path-averaged Stokes feedback.

The principal chain is

$$
\text{conditions}
\longrightarrow \rho_0
\longrightarrow \delta\rho_{\mathrm{RF}}(\omega)
\longrightarrow \delta\mathbf S(\omega)
\longrightarrow \{\delta\phi,\delta\chi,\delta T\}.
$$

## Uniform steady state {#uniform-steady-state}

All active pumps contribute to one zero-RF steady state for each alkali species. The model does not resolve transverse beam profiles or atomic trajectories. In the current physical-pump readout, the RF-induced perturbation is also represented by one density matrix shared by the full optical path.

Uniform does not mean that the entered optical intensity is reduced to a cell average. The configured intensity is used directly in optical pumping, light shifts, and physical-pump feedback.

## Weak-RF expansion {#weak-rf-expansion}

The RF calculation expands the density matrix around zero RF drive:

$$
\rho(t)=\rho_0+\Omega_{\mathrm{rf}}\rho^{(1)}(t)
+\mathcal O(\Omega_{\mathrm{rf}}^2).
$$

Every plotted RF curve is therefore a susceptibility per unit RF Rabi frequency, or a converted response per unit magnetic field. RF saturation and finite-drive power broadening are outside the model.
